summary: KnowFeat is a ReAct agent (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) that writes Python feature-engineering code for tabular ML. It gets structured domain-knowledge cards (risk indicators, detection rules, expert opinions, court evidence, each with an ID). Candidates pass a gate of code execution, noise-calibrated IV/KS statistics and XGBoost delta-AUC, and accepted features carry a provenance card citing the knowledge IDs. On 12 OpenML datasets it has the best average rank, but its gains over no feature engineering are small and within bootstrap CIs except on churn. Its own ablation shows the knowledge cards add 0.8 pp or less over schema metadata.

claims.claim: KnowFeat ranks first (avg. rank 2.3) across twelve public benchmarks among seven methods (one-sided Wilcoxon p=0.017)
claims.evidence: Table III shows average rank 2.3 vs 3.8. The Wilcoxon test compares KnowFeat to No-FE only, not to the competing methods. The median gain over No-FE is +0.25 pp, and bootstrap CIs overlap No-FE on 11 of 12 datasets (Table XIII). Competitors run on different LLM backbones (GPT-5.6-Luna, GPT-5.4-mini vs DeepSeek-V4-Flash).

claims.claim: Peak gain of +11.6 pp AUC on a telecom churn dataset
claims.evidence: Table III: 0.737 to 0.853 on a single frozen split. Churn is one of the four datasets given schema metadata only (§IV-A), so the peak gain involves no domain knowledge. The limitations section says semantic-dimension naming changes churn results substantially.

claims.claim: Structured domain knowledge adds discriminative value
claims.evidence: Table VII, schema-only vs full knowledge: +0.8, +0.3, +0.1 AUC and -0.2 F1. Table VIII: single knowledge types often beat 'full' (credit_g +EXP 0.834 vs full 0.752). The authors themselves conclude that 'the verification pipeline, not knowledge completeness, is the primary quality mechanism'.

claims.claim: On AML datasets KnowFeat maintains competitive detection with full provenance
claims.evidence: SimECNY F1 0.971 = No-FE 0.971 (Table VI); Elliptic AUC 0.9982 vs 0.9981. So it matches, but does not improve.

claims.claim: Provenance cards cut compliance review time from 2-3 hours to 15-30 minutes per feature
claims.evidence: Informal feedback from the co-authoring bank's department; no study design, sample or measurement.

patterns.note: Isolating comparison exists: schema metadata vs schema plus curated knowledge cards, with the same agent and verification gate. Gains are 0.1-0.8 pp AUC (-0.2 F1 on AML), smaller than the 3-run spread on credit_g (0.735-0.774). The largest gain in the paper (churn) used no domain cards. Off-domain (tabular ML), but it is evidence that curated domain context adds little once a strong verification gate exists.
Each artifact links to knowledge IDs plus verification results. The links are the LLM's self-declared reasoning chain, not verified, and the review-time benefit is anecdotal.

L1 execution, L2 statistics and L3 model-delta gate. The authors credit it for stability (3 runs, disjoint feature sets, similar AUC), but there is no no-gate arm. The FeatLLM comparison differs in the generator too, as the authors note.
Failure memory of rejected candidates injected into the prompt; not ablated.

methodology.sample: 12 OpenML/UCI tabular datasets (522 to 48,842 rows), synthetic SimECNY (200K), Elliptic (46K)
methodology.baselines: No-FE, OpenFE, AutoFeat, CAAFE, FeatLLM, LLM-FE, all re-run under the authors' held-out protocol but with different LLM backbones
methodology.models: DeepSeek-V4-Flash agent (Pro swap on 2 datasets); XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost for evaluation
methodology.variance: 5 XGBoost seeds; bootstrap CIs vs No-FE only; 3 end-to-end LLM runs on 2 datasets
methodology.ablations: Schema-only vs full knowledge on 4 datasets; per-knowledge-type on 5
methodology.contamination_controls: Frozen 20% test split never touched during generation (a real improvement over prior work); public datasets are likely in LLM pretraining

standards.artifacts: Code, knowledge bases, feature matrices and evaluation scripts on GitHub; datasets on Hugging Face (anonymous)

biases.detail: The significance test is against No-FE but is presented next to a seven-method ranking.
LLM baselines use different models from KnowFeat, so differences mix method and model.
One agent LLM; a backbone swap on two datasets gives mixed results.
The review-time reduction is informal partner feedback.
'Ruling out an outlier-driven result', and 'confirming overall benefit' from a 0.928 vs 0.925 comparison.

coi.affiliations: East China Normal University, Tsinghua, SWUFE, Postal Savings Bank of China (Digital Currency Department)
coi.detail: A co-author's bank supplies the synthetic AML benchmark and the practitioner feedback; no commercial product is evaluated.

verdict_reason: Off-topic for this KB: automated feature engineering for tabular ML, not software development or the developer's side of it. Within its own scope, the headline 'knowledge-guided' framing is undercut by its ablation, and the peak gain comes from a no-knowledge configuration.
applicability: Does not transfer as software-engineering evidence. One indirect data point for P39: with a strong automated verification gate, curated domain-knowledge cards added at most 0.8 pp over bare schema metadata. A healthcare-education team should therefore not expect glossaries or ontologies alone to move agent outcomes, and should build the checks first. The provenance-card idea (each artifact cites the knowledge IDs it used) is a cheap P42 practice, but here the links are LLM-asserted, not verified.

conflicts_with.detail: The DABStep context-layer ablation finds the semantic content of a data contract does most of the work. Here curated domain knowledge adds 0.8 pp or less over schema metadata and the verification gate is credited instead. The tasks differ (text-to-SQL analytics vs feature search with a model-delta gate).
